description: Realigns Inc is building an offline-first astronaut health monitoring solution for long-duration space missions. Our team focuses on local AI, software engineering, health-data visualization, privacy, and resilient systems.
summary:
ASTRAHEALTH is an offline-first astronaut health research prototype developed by Realigns Inc for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The application integrates historical NASA biomedical measurements, crew health timelines, archived radiation observations, environmental data, and scientific evidence traceability into a single desktop interface.

Using NASA Open Science Data Repository evidence, ASTRAHEALTH enables retrospective health-indicator review, reference-based comparisons, source provenance inspection, and scientific PDF reporting.

The prototype also demonstrates local AI text generation using Qwen2.5-0.5B, with AI-generated explanations clearly labeled as unverified and separated from original scientific measurements.

Built with Electron, React, TypeScript, and SQLite, ASTRAHEALTH demonstrates how evidence-aware astronaut health research software can operate without continuous internet connectivity.

The current prototype is designed for retrospective scientific evaluation, not live spacecraft telemetry, medical diagnosis, or flight-qualified health monitoring.
details:
NASA ASTRAHEALTH- Offline Astronaut Health Intelligence

Developed by Realigns Inc | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

The Challenge

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to complex health challenges involving radiation, altered gravity, physiological changes, isolation, and environmental conditions.

Scientific information relevant to astronaut health is distributed across multiple datasets. Reviewing it requires careful attention to measurement units, sampling times, original sources, and limitations.

Our Solution

ASTRAHEALTH is an offline-first desktop research prototype that brings historical space-health evidence, scientific visualization, and source traceability into one integrated application.

It demonstrates how health-related observations can be organized and reviewed locally without depending on continuous internet connectivity.

Implemented Features

Crew Health: Explore historical Inspiration4 complete blood count measurements, including hemoglobin, red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and other recorded indicators.

Health Timeline: Review observations across seven recorded historical sampling timepoints.

Evidence Explorer: Inspect registered source-file references, measurement classifications, units, and recorded SHA-256 provenance.

Radiation Monitor: Review archived ISS radiation research observations. These are historical measurements, not live personal dosimetry.

Environment Monitor: Compare historical ISS and ground temperature, relative humidity, and CO₂ observations from Rodent Research-1.

Alerts and Mission Replay: Present historical reference classifications and navigate recorded observations without representing them as operational medical alerts or live telemetry.

Scientific Reports: Generate retrospective reports with measurement tables, source information, scientific limitations, and PDF export.

Local AI: Demonstrate offline text generation using Qwen2.5-0.5B and a packaged local inference runtime. Two consecutive generation requests were successful during macOS ARM64 testing. AI-generated responses are labeled unverified and remain separate from source records.

NASA Scientific Evidence

The evaluated prototype uses NASA Open Science Data Repository Inspiration4 OSD-569 complete blood count records, historical Rodent Research-1 environmental observations, and archived NASA RadLab ISS radiation research.

The inspected local evidence registry contains 560 CBC measurement records and 72,522 environmental observations.

Historical biological measurements and environmental observations are kept scientifically separate. The application does not create artificial astronaut measurements to fill missing data.

Technical Architecture

ASTRAHEALTH is implemented with Electron 44, React, TypeScript, Node.js, and local SQLite storage. Local language-model inference uses a packaged llama.cpp-based runtime and a GGUF model.

The architecture emphasizes offline operation, controlled Electron interfaces, local scientific records, explicit model activation, and source-aware presentation.

The final automated evaluation completed 563 tests across 97 test files, with zero failures. The macOS ARM64 application was packaged successfully, and a retrospective scientific report was exported and reviewed.

Innovation and Potential Impact

ASTRAHEALTH combines historical biomedical evidence, environmental research, radiation observations, scientific provenance, and experimental offline AI in a unified desktop interface.

Its contribution is an evidence-aware approach to presenting space-health information while preserving the distinction between observations, derived presentations, unavailable information, and AI-generated explanations.

Future development could extend this foundation with validated health-monitoring inputs, astronaut-centered workflows, and carefully evaluated decision-support functionality.

Limitations and Verification

ASTRAHEALTH is a retrospective scientific research prototype. It does not provide live spacecraft telemetry, certified medical diagnosis, astronaut-specific treatment recommendations, or flight-qualified monitoring.

Local AI generation has been demonstrated, but response completeness, broader reliability, and restart behavior require additional testing. Windows and Linux packaged acceptance and cross-machine installation are also pending.

The project website includes the demonstration, scientific report, supporting references, and verification information.

ASTRAHEALTH is independently developed by Realigns Inc. It is not NASA-endorsed, flight-qualified, or medically certified.
